entries.doesNotDo: It improves nothing about accuracy. Telling the same thing three times faster makes delivery smoother and leaves the errors intact.

entries.name: Shadowing
entries.doesNotDo: It never asks you to choose a word. Following a voice at a delay is articulation practice, not retrieval, and it can be done with very little comprehension.

entries.name: Retelling what you just read
entries.trains: production, and the link from input to output
entries.doesNotDo: It borrows the source's vocabulary. What comes out is partly the text's phrasing echoed back, so it overstates what you can say unprompted.

entries.name: Self-talk — describe what you see
entries.doesNotDo: Nobody corrects you. Errors repeated aloud in private get rehearsed as readily as correct forms do.

entries.name: Describing a picture
entries.doesNotDo: It stays in the present tense and the third person. Pictures rarely require you to narrate, hypothesise or argue.

entries.name: A voice message to a real person
entries.doesNotDo: It cannot be scheduled around your weak forms. You will say what you needed to say, which is the value and also why it trains nothing in particular.

entries.name: Role play or drama
entries.doesNotDo: It needs other people, so it cannot be the thing you fall back on. A method that requires company is unavailable most of the time by construction.

entries.name: Reciting a memorised poem or monologue
entries.doesNotDo: It is recall of one fixed string. Nothing in it generalises to a sentence you have not memorised.

entries.name: Singing along
entries.doesNotDo: Song rhythm overrides speech rhythm. Stress and vowel length get bent to the melody, so the prosody you practise is not the prosody you need.

entries.name: Interpreting for someone
entries.doesNotDo: It overloads before it teaches. Below a working command of both directions it produces failure rather than practice.
